Q: GetX BottomSheet UI not updating when controller update() is called (without using Obx) A:

  1. The GetBuilder inside MainScreen is registered normally

  2. The GetBuilder inside Get.bottomSheet() is **sometimes not properly registered for rebuilds
    **
    When update() is called:

    • Main screen rebuilds ✅

    • BottomSheet GetBuilder may miss the rebuild ❌

      Use id -based updates

      You must explicitly target the BottomSheet rebuild.

      GetBuilder<FilterController>(
  id: 'bottomSheet',
  builder: (controller) {
    return Container(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
      child: Column(
        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
        children: [
          SfSlider(
            min: 0.0,
            max: 100.0,
            value: controller.kmValue,
            showLabels: true,
            showTicks: true,
            onChanged: controller.onChangeKm,
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          Text('Selected: ${controller.kmValue.toInt()} KM'),
        ],
      ),
    );
  },
)


      void onChangeKm(double value) {
  kmValue = value;
  update(['bottomSheet']);
}

      Your code is correct, but GetBuilder needs IDs when used inside BottomSheet overlays.
      update() alone is not enough for overlay widgets.

Q: XDG base dir spec: What to do if $HOME is also not set? A:

In the XDG base dir specification it is advised that if e.g. $XDG_STATE_HOME is not set, the application should fall back to $HOME/.local/state .

I know that the spec uses "should" here, but I have always considered that a matter of its somewhat informal writing style. I would consider an application that did differently to be deviating from the spec, making use of this default value a conformance requirement. "It is advised" does not do justice to that.

But it says nothing about what happens if $HOME is not set. In this case what happens?

A whole lot of things work poorly if HOME is not set. That situation is possible, but most abnormal, especially for a user session. You do well to avoid making assumptions about HOME being defined, but don't overthink it.

Should I check if $HOME is set in my application and if not error out? Or just let the application crash?

The spec does not say. It is therefore likely that application behavior will vary. The behavior is literally undefined.

Personally, if I were not writing a shell script to begin with, I would probably emulate the shell's behavior: references to unset environment variables silently expand to nothing. Thus, in a case where HOME was not set, $HOME/.local/state would expand to /.local/state. That's unlikely to exist, much less to be writable to an ordinary user, but that's not necessarily a problem for base dir. And if there is a problem, then handling a file not found error is better than, say, crashing with a segfault. According to me.

Or should I, in case its not set, fall back further to ~/.local/state ?

Funny that you suggest that. Remember "a whole lot of things work poorly"? One of them is tilde expansion, which is defined in terms of the value of HOME. In terms of the shell, you haven't actually suggested something different.

You do as seems best to you, but as for me, I would not make an heroic effort here.

Q: tflite-runtime ValueError: Didn't find op for builtin opcode 'FULLY_CONNECTED' version '12'. An older version of this builtin might be supported A:

The runtime you are using is too old for the models you trained. Since you used TensorFlow 2.19 and the models are using a newer version 12 operator that your current runtime (v2.13) does not know how to read. You can fix it by switching to LiteRT from ai-edge-litert. It is the modern replacement for tflite-runtime and is updated to support these newer operators.

pip uninstall tflite-runtime
pip install ai-edge-litert 

from ai_edge_litert.interpreter import Interpreter
interpreter = Interpreter(model_path="model.tflite")

Q: PowerBi query for JIRA tickets giving results in loop A:

You're using the REST API endpoint incorrectly. If you refer to the documentation for the Search for issues using JQL enhanced search endpoint, you'll see it does not support the use of any parameter called startAt for performing pagination. That parameter was associated with the previous JQL search endpoints that were deprecated almost one and half years ago, as per CHANGE-2046.

I recommend that you try a public AI again for advice on how to do pagination with the new JQL search endpoints correctly, as the topic has already been extensively documented by Atlassian in How-To articles such as this one, and has been discussed extensively on many forums, such as in the Jira section of the Atlassian Community forum, over the past year and is now considered to be 'common knowledge'.

PS. Your JQL statement is incorrect as well, as you declared:

&fields=summary,duedate,status,assignee,issuetype,project

towards the end of the JQL, and ampersands (&) cannot be used to join clauses, only the word AND can be used. Putting that ampersand there invalidated the remainder of the statement.
